name: irregular verbs
title: Spanish Irregular Verbs Practice: Present and Preterite Quiz
description: Practice Spanish irregular verbs: ser, ir, tener, hacer, decir, poder, venir and yo-go verbs in the present and preterite, with 10 sentences checked as you tap.
answer: Spanish irregular verbs change their stem or endings. In the present, many are irregular only in yo (tengo, hago, pongo, salgo, conozco); others change their stem (quiero, puedo, pido). In the preterite, a key group takes a new stem and unstressed endings: tuve, hice, dije, pude, quise, vine, estuve. Ser and ir share the preterite: fui, fue, fueron.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127b.csv

rules.example: tengo, hago, pongo, salgo, traigo, conozco

rules.use: Stem change e → ie, o → ue, e → i

rules.example: tuve, estuve, pude, puse, supe, quise, vine, hice

quiz.why: Tener is a yo-go verb: tengo.

quiz.after: venir a mi fiesta el sábado?
quiz.why: Poder changes o to ue: puedes.

quiz.after: ir al cine, pero no hay boletos.
quiz.why: No stem change in nosotros: queremos.
Preterite of hacer in yo: hice, no accent.
Preterite stem of venir: vin-, so vinieron.
A completed trip: preterite of ir, fuimos.
After j, the ending is -eron: trajeron.

mistakes: Regularizing yo forms: «yo hacio» and «yo poneo» should be «hago» and «pongo».
Adding accents to the preterite irregulars: «hice», «tuvo» and «dijo» have no written accent.
Changing the stem in nosotros: «podemos», «queremos», «pedimos» keep the infinitive stem.
Writing -ieron after j: «dijieron» and «trajieron» should be «dijeron» and «trajeron».
Mixing up fue: it is both «he/she went» and «he/she was»; context tells which.

heritage: Heritage speakers often use regularized or regional forms in speech, like «trajieron», «dijistes» or «haiga». They are part of real Spanish, but written and exam Spanish expect «trajeron», «dijiste» and «haya». Focus your writing practice on those few forms.
teacher: Divide the board into the patterns in the table and give teams verb cards. They place each verb under its pattern and then write one sentence with it in the preterite.

faq.question: Which Spanish irregular verbs should I learn first?
faq.answer: Ser, estar, ir, tener, hacer, decir, poder, querer, venir and saber. They are among the most frequent verbs in the language and cover the main irregular patterns.

faq.question: Are irregular verbs irregular in every tense?
faq.answer: No. Many are irregular only in yo of the present (tengo, salgo), in the present stem (quiero) or in the preterite (tuve). The imperfect has only three irregular verbs: ser, ir and ver.

faq.question: Why do some preterite forms have no accent?
faq.answer: The irregular preterite stems (tuv-, hic-, dij-, pud-) take endings stressed on the stem: tuve, hizo, dijo. Since the stress falls where Spanish expects it, no written accent is needed.
